Triage: lands in the better-auth bridge / session resolution (`plugin-auth` hooks, `runtime/src/security/resolve-session-principal.ts` seam) ⇒ `domain:identity`; type **Bug** (a 200 no-op on a security endpoint violates the endpoint's declared contract). Dedup: only card in this repo for the class (objectui#4467 is the console half, objectui#4304 closed as its duplicate). ⇒ `needs-user-decision` — auth-flow shape is on the human floor, and the card's two remedies differ in client-visible contract.

**Options** (from the card, sharpened):
- **A. Reject** a bearer-authenticated `impersonate-user` (force clients through the cookie/rotation path). Loud, but the server has no signal for "this caller can adopt the rotation", so practical A = always reject — which breaks impersonation in cookie-blocked deployments, the exact context `bearer()` exists for.
- **B. Rotate/invalidate the caller's bearer as part of impersonation**, so the impersonated session is the only one that resolves afterwards; symmetrically, let `stop-impersonating` honor a bearer-carried recovery (today it resolves the admin via the `admin_session` cookie only, so the exit path is dead in cookie-blocked deployments).

**Recommendation: B**, including the `stop-impersonating` half.

- **Platform long-term coherence:** B closes the class server-side for every client lane; A only re-routes it and leaves cookie-blocked deployments without impersonation at all.
- **Measured business pull:** live — the console (a bearer client after every normal sign-in) got a silent no-op on a security-relevant admin action, with writes mis-attributed to the admin.
- **AI-agent error-resistance:** B makes "impersonation succeeded but did not take effect" structurally impossible; a client that ignores the rotation gets a loud 401, versus today's silently wrong identity on every subsequent write.
- **Startup scope discipline:** one mechanism on an existing endpoint pair, no new declared surface.

## Maintainer ruling — rotation-based invalidation

Ruled by the maintainer in a live PM session, 2026-08-13 (session `session_015XyMgCSMGGn9oSwbQEeWYg`), verbatim: 「其他全部接受你的建议。」 — accepting the rotation direction as recommended.

**Ruling: rotation, not refusal.** `POST /admin/impersonate-user` must **invalidate/rotate the caller's bearer as part of impersonation**, so the impersonated session is the only one that resolves afterwards — "impersonation succeeded but did not take effect" becomes structurally impossible server-side. Refusal-based hardening is rejected: it would leave cookie-blocked deployments (the exact context `bearer()` exists for) permanently unable to impersonate. Additionally ruled: **`stop-impersonating` must honour a bearer-carried `admin_session` recovery**, not the cookie alone — otherwise the exit path cannot work in the deployments this card is about.

**Implementation notes for dispatch:**
- This wraps vendor internals (better-auth 1.7.0-rc.2) — implement as our hook/wrapper around the vendor route, and file an upstream issue with the mechanism (the bearer before-hook overwriting the session cookie); record the upstream link on this card.
- Coverage pins both directions: bearer client impersonates → subsequent bearer requests resolve to the impersonated principal (never the admin); stop-impersonating recovers the admin via bearer.
- Defence-in-depth companion: objectui#4467 option A (console adopts `set-auth-token` rotation) is the client half and stands regardless.

Label swap: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

**Title:**

`bearer() + admin impersonation collide: /admin/impersonate-user returns 200 and is a silent no-op for every bearer client`

**Body:**

> ## Summary
>
> For a client authenticating with `Authorization: Bearer`, `POST /admin/impersonate-user` returns **HTTP 200, creates the impersonation session, emits the impersonated token on `set-auth-token` — and has no effect on any subsequent request.** Every following bearer-authenticated request still resolves to the **admin**, including writes.
>
> Measured on `better-auth@1.7.0-rc.2` (originally observed on 1.6.26 — the mechanism is unchanged between them).
>
> ## Mechanism
>
> Two pieces that are individually correct compose badly.
>
> 1. `bearer()`'s before-hook authenticates a request by **overwriting the request's session cookie** with the bearer token — `dist/plugins/bearer/index.mjs`:
>
>    ```js
>    const existingHeaders = c.request?.headers || c.headers;
>    const headers = new Headers({ ...Object.fromEntries(existingHeaders?.entries()) });
>    setRequestCookie(headers, c.context.authCookies.sessionToken.name, decodedToken);
>    return { context: { headers } };
>    ```
>
> 2. The admin plugin's `impersonateUser` does the opposite — it delivers the new identity **as a cookie** (`dist/plugins/admin/routes.mjs`):
>
>    ```js
>    const session = await ctx.context.internalAdapter.createSession(targetUser.id, true, { impersonatedBy: ... }, true);
>    deleteSessionCookie(ctx);
>    await ctx.setSignedCookie(adminCookieProp.name, `${ctx.context.session.session.token}:${dontRememberMeCookie || ""}`, ...);
>    await setSessionCookie(ctx, { session, user: targetUser }, true);
>    ```
>
> A browser composes these: its cookie jar is updated, so the next request carries the impersonation session. A bearer client cannot. It keeps replaying the same `Authorization` header it was already holding — the **admin's** token — and step 1 keeps converting that back into the admin's session cookie on every request. The impersonation cookie is never read.
>
> Crucially, the admin's own session row is deliberately **kept alive** by `impersonateUser` (parked in `admin_session` for the exit path), so the stale bearer stays valid indefinitely.
>
> ## Why this is worse than a plain bug
>
> Nothing reports it. The endpoint answers 200, the impersonation session row exists, and `set-auth-token` carries a correct impersonated token. Only the *identity of subsequent requests* is wrong — so a caller that checks the response, or a test that asserts the endpoint returns 200 and that a session was created, sees a completely healthy impersonation while every action taken "as the user" is attributed to the admin.
>
> ## Reproduction
>
> 1. Enable `bearer()` and `admin()`.
> 2. Sign in as a platform admin; take the token from the `set-auth-token` response header. Call it `adminToken`.
> 3. `POST /admin/impersonate-user` with `Authorization: Bearer` + `adminToken`, body `{ "userId": "some-other-user" }` -> 200.
> 4. `GET /get-session` with `Authorization: Bearer` + `adminToken` (i.e. the client has not adopted the rotation).
>
> **Expected:** not the admin — either the impersonated user, or a failure.
> **Actual:** the admin, every time.
>
> Step 4 is the whole bug: a client that does not notice `set-auth-token` on the impersonation response is silently un-impersonated rather than loudly broken.
>
> ## Secondary: the exit path is unreachable in the same deployments
>
> `stopImpersonating` resolves the admin through the `admin_session` **cookie only**:
>
> ```js
> const adminCookie = await ctx.getSignedCookie(adminSessionCookie.name, ctx.context.secret);
> if (!adminCookie) throw APIError.fromStatus("INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR", { message: "Failed to find admin session" });
> ```
>
> In a cookie-blocked deployment — the exact context `bearer()` exists for — that cookie never comes back, so even a client that *does* adopt the rotation can never leave impersonation. It gets a 500 with no recoverable state. So the two halves need fixing together: an entry path without a working exit is not usable.
>
> ## Suggested direction
>
> We shipped a fix in our own wrapper (no fork), and it may be worth doing upstream:
>
> - On a **bearer-authenticated** `impersonate-user`, rotate the caller's session as part of impersonating: mint a replacement admin session, hand it back as a recovery credential, and delete the original. The stale bearer then stops resolving, so a client that ignores `set-auth-token` gets a loud 401 instead of a silently wrong identity, and "impersonation succeeded but did not take effect" becomes structurally impossible.
> - Emit the `admin_session` recovery value on a response header (we used `set-admin-session-token`, mirroring `set-auth-token`, and added it to `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`), and accept it back on a request header in `stopImpersonating` so the exit path works without cookies.
>
> We deliberately did **not** take the other obvious option — rejecting bearer-authenticated impersonation — because the server has no signal for "this caller will adopt the rotation", so in practice it means rejecting always, which leaves cookie-blocked deployments unable to impersonate at all.
>
> Happy to open a PR if you would like this upstream; equally happy to be told a different shape fits the plugin model better.
>
> ## Environment
>
> - `better-auth@1.7.0-rc.2` (also present in 1.6.26)
> - Plugins: `bearer()`, `admin()`, `organization()`, `customSession()`
> - Node 22, non-browser and cross-origin browser clients both affected

**代码两半已落地(PR #8432)。裁定的第三项——上游 issue——⛔ 未完成,已转 #8446 跟踪,不是被遗忘。** `domain:identity` 执行席位,session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`。

本卡随 PR 合并自动关闭,所以在这里留指针,免得读到这张已关闭卡的人以为裁定被完整执行了。

## 已兑现

**① 轮换,而非拒绝。** bearer 认证的 `POST /admin/impersonate-user` 现在轮换调用者的凭据:铸造替代 admin session → 把恢复值交给调用者 → 删除原 session。⚠️ **这个顺序是刻意的**:中途失败会让管理员**仍处于登录态而 impersonation 被拒**,而不是把他锁在外面。

**② `stop-impersonating` 支持 bearer 携带的恢复值**(`x-admin-session-token`),在 `AuthManager.handleRequest` 接缝注入到 Cookie,所以 vendor 路由**原样运行**。

两者都是 vendor 路由外的包装 —— ⛔ 无 fork、无 vendoring、无打补丁的依赖,与裁定一致。

## ⛔ 未兑现:上游提交

裁定原文:

> file an upstream issue with the mechanism (the bearer before-hook overwriting the session cookie); **record the upstream link on this card**

**做不了,是权限不是遗漏。** dev 试了三条路,我复核后同样受阻:

| 尝试 | 结果 |
|:--|:--|
| `issue_write` → `better-auth/better-auth` | `Access denied: repository not configured for this session` |
| `add_repo` | `cross-tier adds are not supported in v1` |
| 认证过的 `api.github.com/repos/better-auth/better-auth` | HTTP 403 |

**正文已拟好、查重已做**(`better-auth#10734` 是另一个 `stopImpersonating` cookie 缺陷,`#9401` 已关闭且是客户端 `useSession` 重新校验,两者都不是本机制),存放在 [本卡评论 5280970591](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/8243#issuecomment-5280970591),可逐字提交。

→ **#8446** 跟踪该动作,标注「需要有上游访问权限的人」。

## 我做的取舍,写明以便追责

我**没有**为等这个上游动作压住 PR。本卡修的是安全端点上的**静默 no-op**:console 每次正常登录后都是 bearer 客户端,对一个安全相关的管理操作拿到 200 而操作实际没生效,后续写入被错误归因到管理员。为一个**我们无权执行**的动作压住修复,等于让真实缺陷停留在无法预期何时解锁的窗口里。这个判断是我的。

## 两条 dev 报的诚实边界,供后续参考

- **动态 baseURL 边缘未测**:请求接缝从 `auth.$context` 推导 `admin_session` cookie 名,而 better-auth 在 baseURL 动态时按请求重新推导。前缀不匹配会让恢复头静默不匹配 —— 但 vendor 路由随后走它既有的**大声 500**,⚠️ **永远不会给出错误身份**。失败方向安全,路径未测,已写进代码注释。
- **未做浏览器验证**:客户端那一半是 **objectui#4467 选项 A**(console 采纳 `set-auth-token` 轮换),明确不在本卡范围,且裁定说它「stands regardless」。本 PR 的证据是真实 better-auth 管线端到端,不是活的 console。

## 值得记住的一处测试构造

覆盖 pin **不问状态码,而是问身份** —— 通过 `auth.api.getSession({ headers })`,那正是 `runtime/src/security/resolve-session-principal.ts` 实际调用的东西。对旧 admin bearer **同时**断言 `not.toBe(adminId)` 和 `toBeNull`,这样一个「谁也解析不出」的坏管线无法只靠前者蒙混。消融表里 4 条在突变下仍绿的断言被明确标注为**对照而非 pin**,并附判词:「只断言『impersonation 返回了 200』的测试,面对这个缺陷会是绿的」——那正是本卡缺陷的形状。
